# ACR Drift Report — RiverCity Metro Rider Portal

**Prior:** rcm-2026q3 ACR, product version 2026.3, issued 2026-07-28
**Current:** rcm-2027q1 ACR, product version 2027.1, issued 2027-02-19
**Prepared for:** RiverCity Metro Authority, Office of Civil Rights
**Prepared by:** Meridian Digital Accessibility (Dana Okafor)

---

## 1. What this report is, and what it is not

This is a **document-to-document drift report**. It compares two Accessibility Conformance Reports for the same product across two evaluation cycles. It reads documents. **Nothing was tested for this request, nothing was verified, and neither document was modified.** The rcm-2027q1 evaluation is finished and delivered; its evidence is quoted here as the current cycle recorded it.

**Pair classification: self-produced.** The adherence notes in *both* documents carry `finding_id` and `fingerprint` values traceable to this engagement's evidence spine. That is what makes the finding-level trend table in §5 legal. Against a foreign pair — a vendor's two ACRs, or any pre-fingerprint document — this report would stop at the SC-level term table and carry no trend vocabulary at all.

**Comparability at the document level — checked before anything was tabled:**

| Attribute | Prior | Current | Comparable |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product | RiverCity Metro Rider Portal | same | Yes |
| Conformance target | WCAG 2.2 Level AA | same | Yes |
| Catalog | `2.5-edition-wcag-2.2-508-en` | same | Yes |
| Component set | web only; four chapters `disabled` | same | Yes |
| Accessibility support baseline | NVDA/Firefox, VoiceOver/Safari, TalkBack/Chrome, keyboard-only | same | Yes |

All five match, so the two documents can be compared. Had any one of them differed, the correct output would have been a statement to that effect and no diff table.

---

## 2. Sample comparability (mandatory statement)

Two ACRs rest on two sample sets. WCAG-EM's re-evaluation guidance keeps part of the prior sample for comparability and replaces part for coverage, so the sets are expected to differ — and here they do, substantially. Both cycles report the same headline count (11 structured + 1 random + 2 complete processes), which conceals the churn beneath it.

| | Samples |
|---|---|
| **Common to both cycles** | S01 home, S02 trip planner, S03 route schedule, S06 account dashboard, S07 checkout steps 1–2, S08 contact + paratransit application form, S11 title-vi (legacy info-page template), plus complete processes P01 (web) and P02 (native app, non-web) |
| **In the prior cycle only (retired)** | S04 service alerts, S05 fares, S09 news article, S10 accessibility policy, R01 /riders/lost-and-found |
| **In the current cycle only (added)** | S12 alerts subscription (template shipped 2026-11), S13 fare calculator (rebuilt 2026-10), S14 station detail (template shipped 2026-12), S15 news index (replacing the 2026 news article template), R02 /riders/bike-racks |

Seven of eleven structured samples and both complete processes carried over. Four structured samples were retired and four added; the random sample rotated (R01 → R02, and the sitemap frame itself grew from 214 to 251 URLs).

**Consequence for every table below:** a delta is only movement when its evidence lives in a sample both cycles measured. A delta whose evidence lives only in a replaced or newly-added sample is a **coverage change, not movement**, and is marked as such. One row in §4 (2.4.11) is in that category outright; one (2.4.1) is in it in part.

A note on the current document's `evaluation_methods_used` string, which names "7 structured samples and P01 carried over": P02 also carried over, but P02 is the non-web native-app process and this ACR covers the web component only, so naming P01 alone is coherent, not a discrepancy.

---

## 3. Criterion coverage

Both documents carry the identical criterion set: **32 Level A + 24 Level AA = 56 criteria**, including 4.1.1, which WCAG 2.2 removed and the VPAT 2.5 catalog retains.

**No criterion appears in one document and not the other.** No claim was withdrawn and none was newly added. (Had one been, it would carry a row below with the absence named — a withdrawn claim is a delta, never a silent omission.)

---

## 4. SC-level term deltas

Six criteria changed terms. The other fifty are unchanged and appear only in the counts.

| SC | Prior term | Current term | Delta | Comparable? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1.1 Keyboard | `partially-supports` | `supports` | Failure retired | Yes | `a11y_fare_zone_slider_keyboard` (7c1f22ab) verified absent in the current cycle. Prior failure was S07 + both P01 branches — all carried over and re-tested. |
| 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks | `partially-supports` | `does-not-support` | Failing surface expanded from 2 samples to 6; severity raised MINOR → MAJOR | **In part — see note A** | `a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor` (5f77ab02) still present. See also the term question in §7. |
| 3.3.1 Error Identification | `partially-supports` | `supports` | Failure retired | Yes | `a11y_payment_error_association` (c30e51f9) verified absent. Prior failure was the S07 / P01 declined-payment branch — carried over and re-tested. |
| 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose | `does-not-support` | `partially-supports` | Failing surface narrowed from S07 + S08 to S08 alone | Yes | `a11y_form_autocomplete_missing` (44b09ce6) still present on S08. Both samples carried over, so this is measured movement on measured ground. |
| 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Min.) | `supports` | `partially-supports` | First measurement of a surface the prior cycle did not have | **No — see note B** | `a11y_sticky_filterbar_obscures_focus` (3d90c7e1), first observed this cycle on S14. |
| 4.1.3 Status Messages | `partially-supports` | `supports` | Failure retired | Yes | `a11y_purchase_confirm_silent` (e8c2447d) verified absent. Prior failure was the S07 / P01 default branch — carried over and re-tested. |

**Note A — 2.4.1 is comparable in direction, partly coverage in magnitude.** The prior document recorded failures in R01 and S11; the current document records them in S03, S06, S11, S12, S15 and R02. Split those:

- **Movement, comparable:** S03 and S06 were in the prior sample and **passed** 2.4.1 there. They fail now. That is a real regression on ground both cycles measured, and it is what the legacy-shell rollout of 2026-11 did.
- **Coverage, not comparable:** S12, S15 and R02 did not exist in the prior sample, so their failures add breadth to the current picture without saying anything about change.
- **Retired:** R01's prior failure left with the sample. It did not get fixed; it stopped being measured.

The `worsening` trend call in §5 rests on the comparable half alone and does not need the rest.

**Note B — 2.4.11's delta is not movement.** S14 (station detail) shipped 2026-12, after the prior evaluation window closed on 2026-07-28. The prior cycle produced no measurement of this surface at all. Reading `supports` → `partially-supports` as "2.4.11 got worse" would be wrong: a surface that did not exist was built, sampled, and found defective on first measurement. The row belongs in the report — a term did change in a published document — but it is a coverage change, and any summary that counts it as a regression is miscounting.

**1.4.3 is deliberately absent from this table.** Its term is `partially-supports` in both documents, so it carries no SC-level row; manufacturing movement out of a stable term is how a drift report starts flagging everything. Its *failing-sample list* did change (S03 + S09 → S03 + S15), and that change is reported in §5, where it belongs — against the fingerprint, not the term.

---

## 5. Finding-level trend (self-produced pair)

Trend follows the **fingerprint**, never the term. Read the fingerprint first.

| finding_id | fingerprint | SC | Prior | Current | Trend | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `a11y_fare_zone_slider_keyboard` | 7c1f22ab | 2.1.1 | `partially-supports`, CRITICAL, S07 + both P01 branches | absent | **resolved** | Verified absent. The fare-zone slider now exposes a stepper with full keyboard operation; re-tested in both P01 branches and in a driven keyboard session. Both surfaces common to the two cycles. |
| `a11y_payment_error_association` | c30e51f9 | 3.3.1 | `partially-supports`, MAJOR, S07 / P01 declined-payment | absent | **resolved** | Verified absent. The declined-payment message is announced and programmatically associated with its field. Surface common to both cycles. |
| `a11y_purchase_confirm_silent` | e8c2447d | 4.1.3 | `partially-supports`, MAJOR, S07 / P01 confirmation | absent | **resolved** | Verified absent. The confirmation renders into a live region and was announced in the driven session. Surface common to both cycles. |
| `a11y_form_autocomplete_missing` | 44b09ce6 | 1.3.5 | `does-not-support`, MAJOR, S07 + S08 | `partially-supports`, MAJOR, S08 | **improving** | Still present on a smaller surface: S07's checkout form now carries autocomplete tokens on every applicable field; S08's paratransit application form still carries none. Severity unchanged. Both samples carried over. |
| `a11y_route_badge_contrast` | 2ab9d871 | 1.4.3 | `partially-supports`, MAJOR, S03 + S09 | `partially-supports`, MAJOR, S03 + S15 | **persistent** | Same component, same measurement (2.8:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement), same severity. S03 is common to both cycles and still fails. S09 retired and S15 was added; S15 reuses the same route-badge component, so the changed second sample is sample replacement, not a change in scope. |
| `a11y_swap_button_name` | 91d4e0c3 | 4.1.2 | `partially-supports`, MINOR, S02 | `partially-supports`, MINOR, S02 | **persistent** | Unchanged in scope and severity: the S02 icon-only swap control, on a sample common to both cycles. Origin and destination fields remain directly editable. |
| `a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor` | 5f77ab02 | 2.4.1 | `partially-supports`, MINOR, R01 + S11 | `does-not-support`, MAJOR, S03 S06 S11 S12 S15 R02 | **worsening** | Still present with increased scope *and* increased severity. The comparable evidence is decisive on its own: S03 and S06 passed this criterion in the prior cycle and fail now, following the legacy-shell rollout across the schedules and account areas in 2026-11. S12, S15 and R02 are added samples and contribute breadth, not movement. |
| `a11y_sticky_filterbar_obscures_focus` | 3d90c7e1 | 2.4.11 | — (absent from prior document) | `partially-supports`, MAJOR, S14 | **new** | First appearance. The sticky filter bar on the S14 station-detail template covers focused rows in the departures table. S14 shipped 2026-12 and has no counterpart in the prior sample, so this is first measurement, not regression. |

### Why two rows are not what a term-first reading would make them

- **1.3.5 is `improving`, not `resolved`.** The term moved a full step toward support, which is the shape that most often gets mis-narrated as a fix. The fingerprint is still on the ledger and the paratransit application form still ships without a single autocomplete token. A better term never earns `resolved`; only verified absence does.
- **2.4.1 is `worsening`, not a new finding.** The failing-sample list is almost entirely different from the prior cycle's, which invites filing it as something new. It is the same fingerprint under a rolled-out shell. Reading it as new would lose the history and reset the clock on a defect that has been open since 2026-06.

---

## 6. Summary counts and what they do not mean

**Criteria:** 56 compared (32 A + 24 AA) · 6 terms changed · 50 unchanged · 0 present in one document only.
**Direction of changed terms:** 4 toward greater support (2.1.1, 3.3.1, 4.1.3, 1.3.5) · 2 toward less (2.4.1, 2.4.11).
**Comparability of changed terms:** 4 comparable · 1 comparable in direction only (2.4.1) · 1 not comparable (2.4.11).
**Findings tracked:** 8 · resolved 3 · improving 1 · persistent 2 · worsening 1 · new 1.
**Scope of the whole comparison:** the sampled surface of two evaluations — 7 structured samples plus both complete processes common to the cycles, against 11 structured + 1 random + 2 complete processes measured in each.

**This is not a claim that the product improved.** Four terms moved toward support and two moved away; anyone netting that to "+2" is doing arithmetic the evidence does not support, for three reasons:

1. **Both documents are sample-scoped.** Twelve web samples out of a 251-URL sitemap describe the sampled surface across two scopes. Neither cycle measured the product, and two sample-scoped documents subtracted from each other are still sample-scoped.
2. **One of the two "regressions" is not one.** 2.4.11 is first measurement of a template that did not exist last cycle (note B). Counting it against the product is as wrong as counting it for it.
3. **Row counts equalize things that are not equal.** Three of the four improvements are the same flow: the checkout process and its purchase confirmation, all within S07 / P01. That is one team's remediation of one journey, and it is real work — the CRITICAL keyboard trap on the fare-zone slider is genuinely gone. Against it, the skip-link regression now fails half the current sample across five templates and the random draw, and its severity doubled. One column of ticks does not capture that shape.

**Severity and terms moved on independent axes, as they must.** Severity is an input to *trend* — the evidence contract defines `worsening` partly by increased severity — but it never selects an adherence term. Both cycles here show the axes running free of each other: 2.4.1's term moved because the failing surface grew, while its severity moved because the user impact grew; 1.3.5's term improved a full step while its severity stayed MAJOR, because the people blocked on the paratransit application are blocked exactly as hard as before. If a future cycle shows a term tracking severity, that is a mapping error, not a finding.

---

## 7. Document observations for the owner

Three items surfaced while reading the two documents. None changes a delta above. **This lane does not modify either document**; each of these is the Authority's or the engagement's to resolve.

**A. The current document's 2.4.1 term does not follow from its own note.** The note enumerates failures in S03, S06, S11, S12, S15 and R02 — six of the twelve web samples — and does not state that the criterion is inapplicable to the other six. A mixed pass/fail outcome across a sample set maps to `partially-supports`; `does-not-support` is the term for failure wherever the criterion applies. The catalog's own definition points the same way ("the majority of product functionality does not meet"), and six of twelve is not a majority — the current cycle's evidence table characterizes it as "the majority of the sample," which the arithmetic does not bear out.

The prior document shows the evaluator's own correct handling of this distinction: its 1.3.5 `does-not-support` note reads "fails in S07 and S08 — **every sample where input-purpose fields exist**." That applicability qualifier is precisely what the current 2.4.1 note lacks.

Two things follow. First, my confidence here is bounded: I am reading an adherence note, not the outcome map behind it. If that map records the six unlisted samples as `inapplicable` for 2.4.1, the term is right and only the note needs the qualifier. Second, whichever it is, the finding-level call is unaffected — `a11y_legacy_skiplink_anchor` is `worsening` on the carried-over evidence regardless of which term the document carries. What is affected is the drift narrative a reader takes away: the SC row currently reads as a two-step drop, where the evidence supports a scope expansion inside a mixed outcome. Correcting a term is Lane A work against the engagement record, not something this report does.

**B. Neither document declares a `license`.** The OpenACR schema assumes **CC-BY-4.0 in any output** when the field is absent, so both documents are already published — or publishable — under that license by default rather than by decision. If that is the Authority's intent, set it explicitly; if it is not, it is a live exposure on two issued documents.

**C. Both documents still carry the draft disclaimer.** Both read "Draft for review — not a legally binding conformance claim until reviewed and issued by RiverCity Metro Authority." That language conditions on the Authority's issuance, so it is correct for as long as the Authority has not issued them. Given that the Authority publishes an ACR per major release, the question is concrete: if either document has been published, its disclaimer should have been removed at publication, and a published ACR that still calls itself a draft undercuts the claim it exists to make.

---

## Handoff note — RiverCity Metro Authority, Office of Civil Rights

**What you have.** A drift report over your two delivered ACRs for the Rider Portal: what changed at the criterion level (§4), what happened to each individual defect (§5), and what the numbers do and do not support (§6). The pair is self-produced — both documents carry this engagement's fingerprints — so you get finding-level trend, not just term deltas. Against a vendor's pair of ACRs you could not have this table.

**What it rests on, exactly.** Two documents and two engagement records. **Nothing was tested or verified for this report.** Where §5 says a defect was verified absent, that is the rcm-2027q1 cycle's recorded evidence, read as delivered — I did not re-run the check, and this lane must not. Neither document was validated or re-rendered here; validation belongs to issuance, and both documents were issued.

**The three retirements are the rows that carry publication risk,** because they remove defects from a document you may publish — including a CRITICAL keyboard trap. All three are backed by explicit verified-absent evidence naming the re-test surface and method, and all three surfaces (S07, P01 default branch, P01 declined-payment branch) are common to both cycles, so the review trigger for unbacked retirements does not fire. If you intend to publish rcm-2027q1 as retiring these three, that is the moment an artifact-level spot check of the three re-tests earns its cost — not because anything here looks wrong, but because that is where the claim goes public.

**Your decisions, in priority order:**

1. **2.4.1 — resolve the term question (§7A) before publishing rcm-2027q1.** Check whether the outcome map records the six unlisted samples as inapplicable. If it does, add the applicability qualifier to the note. If it does not, the term should be `partially-supports`. Either way, the defect itself is real, worsening, and now affects half the sample across five templates plus the random draw — the skip-link regression is the single most consequential thing in this comparison, and it is the one item where the document's presentation and its evidence are not yet aligned.
2. **Set the `license` field on both documents (§7B)** — or accept CC-BY-4.0 knowingly.
3. **Decide the disclaimer question (§7C):** if either ACR has been published, remove the draft language from what is published.
4. **Commission remediation on what is still open:** the skip-link anchor (worsening, MAJOR, five templates + random), the route-badge contrast (persistent since 2026-06, 2.8:1), the paratransit form's missing autocomplete tokens (improving but still MAJOR on the form people use to request paratransit service), the new sticky filter bar on station detail (MAJOR), and the trip-planner swap control (persistent, MINOR).

**Routing.** This report files nothing and commissions nothing. The five still-open findings can be converted into filable issues through the bug-reporting path, but they route on the strength of the **rcm-2027q1 evaluation's** evidence — which did test — not on the strength of this diff. Nothing here is a substitute for measurement: no delta in this document was produced by testing anything.

**Boundaries.** This report makes no conformance claim of its own, produces no merged or corrected ACR, and modifies neither input document. Every statement in it is scoped to the samples the two cycles measured. Please do not circulate it, or any count drawn from it, as evidence that the Rider Portal became more accessible — it describes two sampled surfaces, one of which was substantially reconstituted between cycles.
